claims.claim: KMI's structural role is transmission of natural gas and refined products through long-lived network infrastructure; incremental power/data-center load can increase demand for gas transport, while Western Gateway extends refined-products connectivity by combining existing SFPP assets with new-build links.

The bottleneck is not hydrocarbon existence alone but permitted, connected transport capacity; substitution risk rises if power demand is met by non-gas generation or refined-products demand weakens, while successor bottlenecks include permitting, construction and contracted throughput.

causalEdges: power/data-center load -> gas-fired generation need -> natural-gas transport demand -> KMI network utilization
refined-products demand -> western transport constraint -> Western Gateway/SFPP connectivity -> throughput opportunity
permitting/construction delay -> capacity in-service delay -> deferred cash-flow realization
falsifiers: Material data-center/power growth occurs without incremental gas transport demand across KMI-served regions.
Western Gateway fails to secure required approvals/contracts or is cancelled before service.
unknowns: durability of incremental data-center gas demand
KMI net capital commitment to Western Gateway

claims.claim: The available evidence supports project commitment and physical capacity, but does not establish project-level return quality; backlog/FID should not be treated as realized earnings.
Existing-asset contribution can reduce greenfield intensity, but joint-venture execution, permitting, refined-products demand and capital-return realization remain material non-gating risks.
